Figure 1:Given any number of input images and optional camera poses,SplatAnythingreconstructs a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)
representation within seconds. It generalizes across arbitrary scene
scales and camera configurations, while supporting challenging
extrapolated viewpoints. Compared with prior feed-forward 3DGS methods,
SplatAnything achieves substantially stronger cross-scene generalization
and novel-view rendering quality.

Figure 2:Normalization space.(a)Radial Distance Normalizationcanonicalizes a global
radial statistic but leaves Gaussian spacing varying across scenes
and camera configurations, resulting in inconsistent
supervision targets.
(b)Gaussian Spacing Normalizationcanonicalizes a representative statistic of Gaussian spacing, providing a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction.

Figure 3:Architecture of SplatAnything.GivenNNinput images and optional camera parameters,
a frozen geometry foundation model first estimates multi-view
geometry.
We convert the geometry from its native radial-distance-normalized
space to the proposed Gaussian-spacing-normalized space and predict
per-pixel Gaussian attribute through a Gaussian backbone and a lightweight GShead.

Figure 13:Qualitative results of SplatAnything for panoramic images reconstruction. SplatAnything can reconstruct high-quality 3DGS representations from panoramic images with different field of view, demonstrating its strong generalization ability.
Figure 14:More qualitative results of our method. SplatAnything feed-forward reconstructs high-quality 3DGS representations generalizing to arbitrary scenes, scales, and viewpoints in a few seconds.
